_contract: answer_key_contract.md v4.3 — `expected` and `also_accept` are canonical and compared; keys beginning with `_` are never compared.

_why_this_document_matters: The one document in the corpus that fits the schema exactly and creates a record:
an administration date AND an expiry date, both printed, nothing inferred. It is
also the page where every realistic expiry error passes the plausibility check,
which is the empirical argument for the human confirmation step.
meta._page_2: Boilerplate contact block only. No extractable facts. Worth asserting: a model that produces fields sourced to page 2 has hallucinated.

capture_quality.medium: generated PDF with a text layer

pii._why: Anonymised at labelling time, not later. The real-name mapping lives outside version control. Clinical facts (dates, lot, manufacturer, product) are not PII and are kept verbatim so the key can be checked against the page.
pii._open_question: Veterinarian name and licence number are a real, identifiable professional. Licence numbers are matters of public record, but decide deliberately rather than by default — and note that vaccination_record.veterinarian_license_no exists precisely because the health department cares who signed.
pii._household: Same household and same dog as the two Doc Side documents — pseudonyms match those keys exactly.

_migration: Re-keyed from the v1 shape on 2026-09-17. No value was re-labelled. The v4 slots the v1
key did not carry — sex_raw, weight_raw, administered_on_raw, expires_on_raw,
source_region — were filled from the page. v1's 'maps_to_vaccine_code' moved to
`resolution`, where the contract says classification lives.

document._note: The page states no date about itself. 'Date of Rabies Vaccination' is a fact about the vaccination and lives on the line item; 'Invoiced 751512' is a number, not a date.

clinic.name: BetterVet
clinic._phone_note: Printed twice, in two forms: '(888) 788-1165' in the header and '888-788-1165' in the clinic block. Both are faithful transcriptions of one fact, so the clinic-block form is `expected` and the header form is in `also_accept`.
clinic._address_note: Two printed lines — '60 Massachusetts Avenue' / 'Boston, Massachusetts, 02115' — joined with a single space, per contract v4.1. The v4 re-key joined them with ', ', adding a comma the page does not print; the Doc Side invoice key already used a space. Caught by the first model run, which joined them the way the page does.

patient.name: Nutmeg
patient._sex_note: 'SEX: Male' and nothing more. Resolution maps it to dog.sex = male and leaves is_altered NULL: the absence of the word 'neutered' is not evidence of an intact dog.
patient._tag_note: 'Tag Number: 13545' is printed in the vaccination block, not the patient block, so it fills the line-item slot and this one stays null. See the contract on tag_number.

line_items._expires_on_note: Read from 'Next Rabies Vaccination On: 02-28-2025'. The only other date labelled 'Expiration' on the page belongs to the vaccine LOT. See must_not_produce[1].
line_items._manufacturer_note: Captured verbatim, '(INVENTORY)' junk included. Cleaning it is a normalisation decision that belongs downstream of extraction, where the original is still on file to check against.
line_items._veterinarian_note: Named under the signature line as 'Dr. Anna Kate Morgan' with 'License # 7345' beneath. No phone of her own on the page.

also_accept._what: Other transcriptions of the same printed fact that are equally faithful. Compared.

labeled_but_blank._note: 'MICROCHIP:' printed with nothing after it. Jaddi does have one — it is on the Petly record — which makes this a good cross-document consistency case later.

not_present._note: The certificate does not date itself.
The page gives age at vaccination ('12 weeks 5 days'), not a birth date. See must_not_produce[4].
The only phone near the signature is the clinic's. See must_not_produce[6].

must_not_produce.why_tempting: The word 'Expiration' appears exactly once on the page, and it belongs to the vaccine lot, not to the immunity. The real expiry is phrased as 'Next Rabies Vaccination On'.
must_not_produce._arithmetic: 353 days / 30.4375 = 11.60 -> rounds to 12 -> inside rabies range [12, 36]

must_not_produce.why_tempting: IMRAB 3 is a product labelled for three-year duration, so '3' reads as the validity period. But this was an initial dose in a twelve-week-old puppy, which is one year regardless of product — and the page says so twice ('Rabies Vaccine - 1 year', 'Next Rabies Vaccination On: 02-28-2025'). A model that reasons from the product name instead of reading the stated date gets a confidently wrong answer that is two years long.
must_not_produce._arithmetic: 1095 days / 30.4375 = 35.97 -> rounds to 36 -> exactly at the top of range [12, 36]
must_not_produce._note: This is the expensive error. A dog reads 'current' for two years after its rabies protection actually lapsed.

must_not_produce.why_tempting: 29 February 2024 plus one year has no canonical answer. Naive date arithmetic yields 2025-03-01 or 2025-02-28 depending on the library. The page states 02-28-2025 explicitly, so no derivation is needed or wanted.

must_not_produce.source_of_error: 2024-02-29 minus the stated age of 12 weeks 5 days
must_not_produce.why_tempting: Unlike the others, this inference is probably CORRECT — which is exactly when the temptation is strongest and the habit most dangerous. The page states an age, not a birth date. Capture 'age_at_vaccination_raw' and let a human decide whether to write dog.date_of_birth.
must_not_produce._note: This is the same principle as never deriving expires_on, applied to a case where deriving would have worked. The rule earns its keep by being unconditional.

must_not_produce.why_tempting: Three bare integers sit within a few lines of each other — tag 13545, invoice 751512, lot 18583 — and only the labels distinguish them.

must_not_produce.source_of_error: clinic switchboard number in the page header
must_not_produce.why_tempting: It is the only phone number near the signature. It is the clinic's, not the veterinarian's, and the page does not carry hers.

resolution._layer: 2 — the database interprets what the model transcribed. Not part of the model's score.

patient._note: One token, two columns, in both cases. See the Petly key for the 'Spayed Female' / 'Shih Tzu Mix' side of the same split.

schema_outcome._layer: 3 — rows that should exist once a human confirms the extraction.

document.owner_id: <resolved to the owner, NOT the dog — one certificate, one household>

schema_outcome.document_dog: one row, linking the document to this dog

vaccination_record._why: Unlike the Doc Side invoice, this page states an administration date AND an expiry date. Both NOT NULL columns are satisfied from the page, with nothing inferred.

exercises_these_invariants: verification_coherent                 — unverified, so verified_by and verified_at both NULL
flag_validity_plausibility            — 12 months, inside rabies [12, 36], flag stays false
compliance_view_note: The dog was 12 weeks 5 days old at vaccination, under vaccine_type.min_age_weeks = 16
for rabies. v_dog_vaccine_compliance checks 'latest_record_id IS NOT NULL' -> current
BEFORE it checks the not_yet_due age branch, so an early vaccination reads 'current'
rather than 'not yet due'. This document exercises that ordering with a real case.
As of any date after 2025-02-28 this record reads 'expired', which is correct —
there is a later rabies dose on the Doc Side records (03-08-25), and reconciling the
two is the multi-document case worth labelling next.

annotations._never_compared: Anything in this block is documentation.
how_to_use: This file is frozen test data, not logic. It is written once from the page and
never revised, because the page will never change. It is the denominator for
every accuracy claim about the extraction pipeline.
Assert three things against a model run:
1. expected.*        — the model produced these values
2. absent.*          — the model did NOT invent values for these
3. must_not_produce  — the model did NOT produce these specific wrong values
(3) is the one most evaluation harnesses skip, and it is where this document is
interesting: all three realistic expiry errors on this page pass the
vaccination_record.validity_implausible check. Plausibility cannot save you here.
A human looking at the page is the only thing that can.

absent_outside_the_shape._note: Listed as not_present in v1; the canonical shape has no slot for it, so it is not scored.

notes: The three-year rabies and DHPP records on the Petly pages land at exactly 36 implied months, the top of the seeded plausible range. The range is correct but has no headroom — worth knowing before anyone widens or narrows it.
'Manufactuer' is misspelled on the certificate. Field-name matching should be fuzzy; do not encode the typo as an expectation.

Two of the six traps here (1 and 2) yield a value that passes every automated check in the schema. That is the empirical case for the human confirmation step, and it is worth citing in the README by name rather than in the abstract.
